original_context: Order theory: downward-closed or lower set A of partially ordered S; whenever a∈A and q≤a then q∈A, here specializing to rational order.
definition: For a partially ordered set (P,≤), a subset A⊆P is a lower (downward-closed) set if whenever a∈A and p∈P with p≤a, then p∈A.
reasoning: The independently screened Dedekind cut of rationals is an example of a lower set but also requires nonemptiness, properness, and no greatest element. The generic lower-set property on an arbitrary poset is not equivalent to a Dedekind cut or to a ring ideal.

sources.relevance: Directly checked order-theoretic downward-closure criterion; no ring or cut completeness assumptions.

related_screened_meanings.relation: strict specialization to rational order with nonempty/proper/no-largest conditions
uses Dedekind cuts as elements, not general lower sets

comparison.rationale: Compared all 595 screened and 16 provisional meanings, including Dedekind cuts, transfinite order notions, ideals and partially ordered sets. No whole-mathematical-meaning equivalent to an arbitrary downward-closed subset exists. Previous newly staged relation properties are predicates on binary relations, not downward-closed subsets. All 12 previously staged preliminary dispositions were also considered; none is an exact whole-meaning duplicate of this candidate.

mathematical_assumptions: An empty set is lower by vacuity.
The underlying ordering is a partial order; the same predicate generalizes to preorders if typed separately.
No demand for directedness (order-theoretic ideals) or lack of maximal element (Dedekind cuts).
